test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the main purpose of creating DNA copies during reproduction?

options.text: To change the structure of cells
To make organisms immune to diseases
To pass genetic information to offspring

solution:
The correct answer is __**To pass genetic information to offspring**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)** replication is the fundamental process during **reproduction** that ensures the **genetic blueprint** is transferred from one generation to the next.
 
• In a dividing cell, the **nucleus** contains information for the inheritance of features from parents to **offspring** in the form of **DNA** molecules.
 
• The process of **DNA copying** creates two copies of the genetic material; these copies need to be separated from each other, with each going to a new daughter cell.
 
• Simply creating a **DNA copy** is not enough; it must be accompanied by the creation of an additional **cellular apparatus** (like mitochondria, ribosomes, etc.) so that the DNA copies have a functioning environment to survive. ***Hence, the primary purpose is to pass genetic information, making this statement the correct answer.***
 
• The consistency of **DNA copying** during **reproduction** is important for maintaining the **body design** features that allow an organism to use a particular niche.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of DNA:** 
 
 
• **DNA** is a double-stranded **helical structure** first described by **James Watson** and **Francis Crick** in **1953**.
 
• It is composed of **nucleotides**, which consist of a **phosphate group**, a **deoxyribose sugar**, and four types of **nitrogenous bases**: **Adenine (A)**, **Thymine (T)**, **Guanine (G)**, and **Cytosine (C)**.
 
 
 
• **The Role of Variations:**
 
 
• No biochemical process, including **DNA copying**, is **100% accurate**. Small alterations occur during the process, leading to **variations** in the offspring.
 
• These **variations** are the source of **evolution** and allow species to survive in changing environments or **ecological niches** over long periods of **time**.
 
• While drastic changes in DNA can lead to the death of a cell, subtle **variations** provide a competitive advantage in the struggle for survival.
 
 
 
• **Heredity and Genes:**
 
 
• A **gene** is a specific segment of **DNA** that provides information for making a particular **protein**.
 
• If the information in the **DNA** changes, different **proteins** will be made, eventually leading to altered **body designs** or **traits**.
 
• **Heredity** is the process by which **traits** and characteristics are transmitted from **parents** to **progeny** through these **genetic codes**.
 
 
 
• **Modes of Reproduction:**
 
 
• In **asexual reproduction**, a single parent produces **DNA copies** that are almost identical, resulting in **clones** with very little variation.
 
• In **sexual reproduction**, **DNA** from two different individuals combines, leading to a greater degree of **variation** and genetic diversity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location:** In **eukaryotic cells**, the majority of **DNA** is located in the **cell nucleus**, organized into structures called **chromosomes**. A small amount of **DNA** can also be found in **mitochondria** (mtDNA) and **chloroplasts**.
 
• **Cell Division:** Before **mitosis** or **meiosis** begins, the cell enters the **S-phase** (Synthesis phase) of the **cell cycle**, where **DNA replication** occurs.
 
• **Biological Significance:** Without **DNA copying**, the continuity of life would cease because new cells would lack the instructions necessary to perform **metabolic functions** or maintain **biological structures**.
</ul
